posts.content:
A fast fleet can still get stuck in traffic.
 
Two robots want the same aisle. A third is idling on a task that went to a robot on the far side of the floor. None of that is a speed problem.
 
When multiple robots are moving through the same operation, speed alone isn't enough. They need to know where to go, which task to take, and when to change course - without creating congestion along the way.
 
That’s what Addverb’s Fleet Management System, Movect handles. It dynamically assigns tasks, plans efficient paths, manages congestion, and reroutes robots as conditions change - keeping the fleet coordinated as the operation moves.
 
The result is smoother movement, fewer bottlenecks, and a fleet that keeps working at its best. Moving more robots is easy. Coordinating them is the real challenge.

Some operations need fixed automation. Others need flexibility. Many need both. So why should automation be one-size-fits-all?
 
As volumes rise and operations become more complex, limited space and labor constraints can make it harder to keep material moving efficiently. The challenge isn’t simply adding automation. It’s building a system that fits the operation today and can adapt as it changes.
 
Across 350+ clients and 500+ automated warehouses, we’ve seen that no two operations work exactly the same way. That’s why, at Addverb, the right approach often brings together fixed and flexible automation, orchestrated by modular software - configured around the way each operation actually runs.
 
4,500+ robots deployed is a number. What matters is what they enable: more capacity, better efficiency, and room to scale.
 
Automation works best when it fits the operations - not the other way around.

What if a smoother turn could move 70% more?
 
When you’re running a fleet of sortation robots, every turn is repeated hundreds or thousands of times. A small change in how each robot navigates can therefore create a significant impact across the entire operation.
 
That’s what Zippy AGV’s curvilinear-path navigation is designed to do. Instead of stopping at sharp 90° turns, Zippy transitions smoothly between waypoints, helping the fleet maintain flow with fewer interruptions.
 
This small change results in smoother direction transitions, better payload stability, more efficient floor space utilization, and one clear outcome: increased overall throughput- anywhere from 30% to 70% depending on layout.
 
At Addverb, every update is a step toward smarter, more efficient automation. Stay tuned for more - and connect with our experts to know what this means for your robotic fleet.

Boosting AGV uptime with smarter charging - Addverb × STÄUBLI
 
When AGVs stop to charge, the warehouse shouldn’t have to. For Addverb, autonomous charging needed to be fast, reliable, and able to handle real-world docking conditions without adding complexity to the vehicle.
 
That’s where our partnership with Stäubli comes in. The CombiTac align 4 solution enables reliable autonomous charging with built-in misalignment compensation and high-current power contacts, supporting faster charging cycles and higher AGV availability.
 
With up to 100 A charging capacity, ±4 mm radial and ±2° angular compensation, and MULTILAM contact technology designed for repeated mating cycles, the solution is engineered for the demands of automated warehouse operations.
 
The result: shorter charging stops, higher AGV availability, and simpler fleet operations.

posts.content:
Fully automated warehouses aren't the goal for every operation. According to McKinsey, three levels of automation solve different problems and every warehouse fits at least one.
 
Basic Automation includes tools like a Warehouse Management System, conveyors, RF scanners, and pallet wrappers. It helps large-item distribution centres, building-material warehouses, and cross-docks handle everyday operations more efficiently without changing the floor.
 
Point Automation adds systems like AMRs, and AGVs to specific tasks. It works well for warehouses that want to speed up particular workflows - like case-picking in grocery, or moving pallets in an existing distribution centre.
 
Fully Automated Warehouses bring together shuttle systems, high-bay cranes, ASRS, and pick arms as one connected system. Best suited for dark stores, redistribution centres, and micro-fulfilment operations where speed and capacity matter most.
 
No phase is better than another. The right one is the one that solves your biggest operational challenge - and fits where your business is going.
 
Good automation isn't about how much you automate. It's about how well it fits your operation.
 
Framework reference: McKinsey & Company

posts.content:
Aircraft use radar. Ships use sonar. Modern AMRs use LiDAR. Dynamo 200 pairs 3D LiDAR with Addverb's engineering for warehouses that don't stand still.

Every warehouse is a dynamic environment. People move, pallets shift, and workflows change through the day. In these conditions, autonomous navigation alone isn't enough - reliable material movement depends on how well the robot sees what's around it, and how precisely it can transfer between workstations.

That's what Dynamo 200 is built for. 2D LiDAR handles safety perception. 3D LiDAR adds spatial awareness in dynamic environments. And a dual-conveyor system moves two totes at a time - automating material transfer between workstations without slowing down.

With a 200 kg payload, up to 2 m/s travel speed, in-place turning, and ±20 mm docking accuracy, Dynamo 200 fits into warehouse operations that change by the hour - moving material precisely, and keeping the flow uninterrupted.

In warehouses that never stop changing, the robots that keep up are the ones that see the change first.

Warehouse worker injury rates in the US climbed from 4.0 to 5.5 per 100 workers since 2020. Automation is one answer to that trend.
 
Every day, warehouse teams repeat the same storage and retrieval tasks hundreds of times. Lifting, carrying, bending, reaching, and walking become part of every cycle. Each movement is small on its own - but repeated across thousands of shifts, it compounds into ergonomic strain that eventually shows up in injury statistics.
 
Automation isn't about replacing people. It's about removing the most repetitive parts of the job so warehouse teams can focus on work that creates greater value - and stay safer while doing it.
 
Across our portfolio, from mobile robots to multi-carton picking systems like Veloce, Addverb builds automation that takes the load off the operator. Automating repetitive handling. Improving throughput. Maximising storage density. And creating a safer, more ergonomic working environment.
 
The strongest backbones in a warehouse shouldn't have to carry the entire operation.

Source: Bureau of Labor Statistics

From carrying payloads of up to 20 kg to climbing 180 mm steps with 3D LiDAR perception, Jetson Orin computing, and an optional QDD robotic arm, Trakr 20 is designed to inspect, carry, interact, and operate where conventional mobile robots reach their limits.
 
Whether it's inspection, material handling, or navigating challenging environments, Trakr 20 combines stability, intelligence, and mobility to keep operations moving where work actually happens.
 
The future of industrial robotics isn't built for perfect environments. It's built for real ones

Another country. Another industry. Addverb's European footprint is expanding with Peka Kroef B.V., one of Europe's leading producers of fresh chilled potato products, as our newest deployment in the Netherlands.
 
The company continuously invests in innovation, quality, and operational excellence and this next-generation automated warehouse is a key step in supporting their future growth and enhancing service across retail, foodservice, and food industry customers.
 
Our team is on-site, piecing together the systems that will power the operation. The integrated solution brings together Multi-Pro (Mother child shuttle) , Travect (RGV) , Cruiser 360 (4-way pallet shuttle) , pallet lifts and conveyors, engineered to work as a single coordinated flow across storage, movement, and dispatch.
Built for scale from day one. 

More updates to follow as the site comes online.
Looking to automate your warehouse operations? Connect with our experts today.

Addverb is partnering with NABET-QCI and NAMTECH to launch the Warehouse Robotics & Automation System- an 8-week programme built to train the next generation of automation engineers.
 
The programme combines hands-on training with real industry immersion, preparing participants for roles like Robotics Engineer, AMR/AGV Engineer, Automation Engineer, and Warehouse Automation Project Engineer. 

No prior robotics experience needed- just the drive to build what's next.
 The future of warehouse automation runs on the people who know how to build it. This is where that pipeline starts.

To know more and join the programme, visit the link in the comments.
